label: Britain Falls, America Stands Alone
detail: The United States was not yet at war in November 1940, so the nearest version of an American defeat is this: Britain loses the Battle of Britain and capitulates in October, leaving the country to face a victorious Germany, Italy and Japan alone.
assumption: A lost American war cannot have happened by election day. Instead, Axis victory in Europe is complete before the vote: Britain is invaded and accepts an armistice. Voters respond to a sharply heightened sense of national danger and to the collapse of the aid-to-Britain policy.
facts_text: In September 1940 the German air force broke the Royal Air Force, and German troops landed on the southern coast of England.
On 12 October 1940 the British government in London accepted an armistice with Germany; the King and part of the Cabinet have gone to Canada, and the fate of the British fleet remains unsettled.
Germany, Italy and Japan, allied by pact since 27 September, now dominate Europe and press in the Far East, and Washington is rushing measures to defend the Western Hemisphere.

add_planks.text: Immediate and complete defense of the Western Hemisphere, including Canada, against the victorious European powers.
Emergency expansion of the Army and Navy and joint defense with Canada and the Latin American republics to hold the hemisphere.

research_questions: How did American public opinion polls in summer 1940 measure expectations of a British defeat, and how did they shift after the fall of France?
Did the fall of France in June 1940 move voters toward the incumbent administration or toward isolationist positions, and which groups moved most?
How did German-American, Italian-American and Irish-American voters react to Axis military successes in 1940?
Do wartime emergencies in other democracies show a rally to sitting governments, or a turn against them?

contradicted.why: Printed the day Britain accepted an armistice, it treats Britain as holding on and needing only more machines, while German troops were already ashore in England.
It calls Britain the lone surviving democracy still fighting and hopes for a victorious Britain a week after Britain signed an armistice.
An editorial titled 'Why We Must Aid Britain' makes no sense after Britain has left the war.
It reports Britain giving military aid to Greece and opening Balkan consultations, which a Britain under armistice with Germany could not do.
It describes Washington as in practical alliance with a fighting England, after England had already accepted an armistice.

consequences: Britain did not win the Battle of Britain: after the German air force broke the Royal Air Force and German troops landed in southern England, the London government accepted an armistice with Germany on 12 October 1940, and the King and part of the Cabinet now carry on from Canada.

No great power is any longer fighting Germany in the west, so the United States faces a victorious Germany, Italy and Japan without an ally, and the fate of the British fleet is the most anxious question in Washington.
Defense of the coasts, of Canada and of the Latin American republics is being rushed, and every fresh call-up and shipyard order is tied to holding the Western Hemisphere.

items.text: BOSTON—Coast artillery National Guard units were ordered today to man the harbor forts at once, a month ahead of schedule. Officers at Fort Banks said searchlight drills will run nightly, and fishing boats were warned to keep clear of the outer harbor channels after dark until further notice.

HALIFAX, N.S.—A steamer crowded with British families, among them several hundred children, docked this morning after a crossing under Canadian naval escort. Relatives from New York and New England met the ship. Canadian officials said further sailings from Irish ports are expected, and they asked American churches for blankets and winter clothing.

DES MOINES—The Navy recruiting station here reports a record week, with 212 young men from Iowa enlisting since Monday. Recruiters said quotas were doubled after word from Washington that new destroyers and cruisers need crews by spring. Applicants must be 17 to 31, and those under 21 need a parent's consent.

Wool and rubber prices rose sharply on the New York exchanges this week, as shipments formerly routed under British control were held in port pending word on Atlantic convoy arrangements. Clothing manufacturers warned that overcoat prices may advance before Christmas.

check.question: What is Britain's position in the European war as of early November 1940?

focus.why: Atlantic seaboard voters who suddenly faced an exposed coast would be the most likely to rally to the sitting administration in a war crisis, as they did after the fall of France.

Irish, German and Italian voters had already drifted from the incumbent over aid to Britain, and an Axis victory could sharpen their wariness of a war-minded administration or soften it once the British cause was gone.
Isolationist Midwestern voters, torn between fear of war and fear of an unprepared country, are those whose choice a direct threat to the hemisphere would most plausibly unsettle.
Pacific Coast voters facing a stronger Japan, now allied with the victors in Europe, would feel the danger of standing alone most directly after the Atlantic coast.

reinterpretation: You asked for America losing the Second World War; this models Britain falling in 1940 instead, since the United States was not yet at war by that election.
